title: Gradient Strain Chip for Stimulating Cellular Behaviors in Cell-laden Hydrogel
protocol: Weigh 10 g of gelatin powder and add it to a glass flask containing 100 mL of Dulbecco's phosphate-buffered saline (DPBS).
Place a magnetic stir bar into the flask and cover with aluminum foil.
Set the hot plate temperature to 50-60 °C and stir at 100 rpm for 1 h to dissolve gelatin powder.
Add 8 mL of methacrylic anhydride very slowly using a pipette.
Let it react at 60 °C for 3 h.
Add pre-warmed DPBS (40 °C) to the flask to reach a final volume of 500 mL and mix well for 15 min.
Cut dialysis membrane into several 25 cm-long tubes and immerse them in deionized water for 15 min.
Load appropriate amount of polymer solution into the dialysis tubes and close one end with a knot.
Place dialysis tubes in a 5-L plastic beaker containing DI water for a week, renewing the water twice daily.
Maintain the solution at 40-50 °C during the dialysis process.
Collect the solution from the tube in a glass bottle.
Pour approximately 450-500 mL of solution into a filter cup with a pore size of 0.22 μm and apply vacuum for sterilization.
Transfer sterilized polymer into several 50-mL sterilized tubes.
Store the tubes in a -80°C freezer for 3 to 5 days.
Freeze-dry the polymer at -80°C using a freeze dryer for 1 week.
Form GelMA and store it in a -80°C freezer.
Cut commercial glass slides into pieces measuring 25 mm x 37.5 mm.
Immerse the slides in 0.5 M NaOH solution for 4 hours.
Wash the slides with deionized water extensively.
Place the slides in a glass container filled with 95% ethanol.
Clean the slides using an ultrasonicator at 43 kHz for 15 minutes.
Air dry the glass slides.
Immerse the slides in a 5% TMSPMA solution in 99.5% ethanol for 1 hour.
Wash the slides with 95% ethanol and air dry them.
Anneal the TMSPMA-coated slides in an oven at 80°C for 2 hours.
Take one 2 mm-thick PMMA plate and apply double-sided tape to one side.
Release the liner on the taped side of the PMMA plate.
Cut a second 2 mm-thick PMMA plate without tape into dimensions of 42 mm x 30 mm.
Laser-cut this plate to serve as the bottom plate of the chip.
Cut another 2 mm-thick PMMA plate with double-sided tape into outer dimensions of 42 mm x 30 mm and inner dimensions of 37.5 mm x 25 mm for the boundary frame.
Laser-cut a 0.3 mm-thick PMMA plate with double-sided tape to form a center circle measuring 12 mm in diameter.
Create two flow channels, each 8 mm long and 2 mm wide, on opposite sides of the central circle.
Assemble three pieces of PMMA components using double-sided tape.
Laser-cut a 2 mm-thick PMMA plate into a 5 cm x 5 cm piece with a 3 x 3 array of 8.5 mm x 8.5 mm hollow rectangles.
Cut another 5 cm x 5 cm piece with a 3 x 3 array of 4-mm hollow circles from the same thickness PMMA plate.
Laser-cut a 1 mm-thick PMMA plate into a 5 cm x 5 cm bottom plate without double-sided tape.
Assemble three pieces of PMMA components using double-sided tape to prepare the mold for casting the PDMS plug.
Mix 30 g of PDMS elastomer with 3 g of PDMS curing agent.
Degas the mixture under a vacuum chamber for 1 hour.
Cast 1.8-2.0 g of degassed mixture into the PMMA mold for the PDMS cover.
Use appropriate amount to fill each cavity of the PMMA mold for the PDMS plug with the degassed mixture.
Cast 10 g of uncured PDMS mixture in a blank 10-cm plastic plate.
Put these molds in a vacuum chamber to degas for 30 minutes.
Cure the PDMS at 80 °C for 2 hours.
Cool down the cured PDMS on the mold after curing.
Detach the PDMS covers and plugs from the PMMA molds.
Punch two holes with diameters of about 3 mm at the ends of flow channels of the PDMS covers.
Cut PDMS sheet into 1 cm x 1 cm cubes.
Punch a 3-mm hole in each PDMS cube.
Glue two uncured 1 cm x 1 cm PDMS cubes onto the openings of the PDMS cover.
Cure for 1 hour at 80°C.
Pre-treat the bonding side of the PDMS cover and the TMSPMA-coated slide under an oxygen plasma machine or a high-frequency electronic corona generator.
Bond the plasma-treated surface of the PDMS covers to the TMSPMA slide by pressing them closely.
Place the chip in an oven at 80°C for 1 hour (optional).
Immerse chips in 95% ethanol for 15 minutes after cooling.
Air dry the chips.
Sterilize the chips under UV irradiation for 1 hour.
Store the sterilized chips in a box wrapped in aluminum foil in the laminar hood.
Prepare 100 mL of DMEM medium with 10% FBS and 1% Pen-Strep, adding 250 mL of DPBS in a 37 °C water bath.
Weigh 25 mg of freeze-dried GelMA into 0.3 mL of prewarmed (37 °C) cell culture medium in a 1.5-mL black microcentrifuge tube.
Stir the mixture until the GelMA dissolves completely.
Weigh 50 mg of photoinitiator into 1 ml of DPBS in a microcentrifuge tube and place it in an 80 °C oven for 15 min or until dissolved.
Take 25 µL of the 10% photoinitiator solution and add it to the GelMA mixture from step 4.3.
Pipette several times to mix well.
Count 3 x 106 NIH 3T3 cells using an automated cell counter.
Centrifuge the suspension at 200 x g for 5 min, discard the supernatant, and re-suspend the cells in 175 µL of cell culture medium.

Add the cell solution from step 4.6 to the microcentrifuge tube containing the GelMA and photoinitiator mixture to form a prepolymer cell solution with 5% GelMA, 0.5% photoinitiator, and ~6 x 106 3T3 cells/mL.
Mix thoroughly.
Load 100 µL of the prepolymer cell solution into a 100-µL micro syringe.
Manually align a piece of the photomask onto the bottom slide of the sterilized gradient strain chip and fix it in place using a small drop of DI water.
Connect the 100-µL micro-syringe loaded with prepolymer cell solution to the inlet of the chip.
Place 50 μL of prepolymer cell solution in the flow channel using a micro-syringe.
Plug the outlet with a PDMS plug.
Inject an extra 40 μL of solution to create a convex bulge in the circular PDMS membrane.
Move the chip, photomask, micro-syringe, and PDMS plug under a UV lamp (365 nm, 9 mW/cm²) and expose it for 30 - 45 seconds to crosslink the concentric circular hydrogel.
Remove the PDMS plug and micro-syringe to release liquid pressure.
Use a 1-mL syringe loaded with prewarmed DPBS to wash uncrosslinked resins three times by flushing from inlet to outlet.
Fill the flow channel with approximately 100 μL of cell culture medium.
Place the chip in a sterilized culture dish and culture it in a 5% CO₂ atmosphere at 37 °C for one week.
Refresh the medium daily.
Take images of three chips on day 0 after 4 hours of incubation, as a control group.
Take images of three chips on day 3, as the experimental set, using a microscope with a 20X objective.
Measure the line width of each hydrogel from line 1 to line 12 using software (e.g., ImageJ) to calculate compress strains.
Use a syringe to inject 4% paraformaldehyde (PFA) in DPBS at room temperature into the flow chip for 15 min for cell fixation.
Replace the PFA solution with 0.5% cell membrane permeating solution in DPBS for 10 min at room temperature to permeabilize the cell membrane.
PBS wash the samples three times, each for 5-10 minutes at room temperature using a loaded syringe.
Load 1% BSA solution into the fluidic channel for 45-60 minutes at room temperature using a loaded syringe through the inlet port.
Add 1.5 mL of methanol to the vial with Alexa Fluor 488 phalloidin to yield a final concentration of 6.6 µM stock solution.
Take 5 µL of Alexa Fluor 488 phalloidin from step and dilute it in 200 µL of DPBS with 0.1% BSA to form a final concentration of 0.165 µM Alexa Fluor 488 phalloidin.
Add 200 µL of the mixture solution to the fluidic channel using a micropipette and incubate the chip at 37 °C for 45-60 min for actin staining.
PBS wash the samples three times, each for 5-10 minutes at room temperature using a loaded syringe.
Prepare 1 µg/mL DAPI in PBS and flow it through the chip to stain cell nuclei at 37 °C for 5 min.
Pipette DPBS into the fluidic channel to wash out the staining solution.
Refill the fluidic chamber with PBS solution to take images with a fluorescence microscope.
Capture fluorescent images of the 3T3 cells in the hydrogels using an inverted fluorescence microscope.
Use a magnification of 40X.
Employ a CCD detector for imaging.
Utilize filter sets with ex/em at 488/520 nm for Alexa Fluor 488 phalloidin (actin).
Use filter sets with ex/em at 358/461 nm for DAPI (nucleus).
